sailfin-lizard.funFact: Un lagarto con vela en la espalda

texas-rat-snake.name: Texas Rat Snake
texas-rat-snake.description: The Texas rat snake is a large, non-venomous colubrid native to Texas and the south-central United States. It is a powerful constrictor that feeds primarily on rodents. It is highly adaptable and found in a wide range of habitats.

gopher-tortoise.name: Gopher Tortoise
gopher-tortoise.description: The gopher tortoise is a keystone species of the southeastern United States, known for digging extensive burrows. These burrows provide critical shelter for over 350 other species, including the eastern indigo snake. It is a slow-moving herbivore.

bush-viper.name: Bush Viper
bush-viper.description: The bush viper is a venomous, arboreal viper found in the tropical rainforests of equatorial Africa. It has distinctive leaf-shaped, keeled scales in various colors. It is nocturnal and uses its prehensile tail to hang from branches while hunting.

pancake-tortoise.name: Pancake Tortoise
pancake-tortoise.description: The pancake tortoise is a critically endangered species with a uniquely flat, flexible shell. Found in the rocky outcrops of East Africa, it wedges itself into crevices when threatened. It is one of the fastest tortoise species relative to its size.

cottonmouth.name: Cottonmouth
cottonmouth.description: The cottonmouth, or water moccasin, is a venomous pit viper found in the wetlands of the southeastern United States. It is the only venomous water snake in North America. It is often found swimming with its head above water.

cuban-crocodile.name: Cuban Crocodile
cuban-crocodile.description: The Cuban crocodile is a critically endangered species found only in the Zapata Swamp and Isle of Youth in Cuba. It is highly aggressive and more terrestrial than other crocodiles. It can gallop on land and is known for its distinctive horned ridges.
cuban-crocodile.funFact: Un cocodrilo en peligro de Cuba

yellow-bellied-slider.name: Yellow-Bellied Slider
yellow-bellied-slider.description: The yellow-bellied slider is a semi-aquatic turtle native to the southeastern United States. It has a dark shell with yellow stripes and a distinctive yellow patch on its plastron. It is one of the most common turtle species in pet trade.

western-diamondback-rattlesnake.name: Western Diamondback Rattlesnake
western-diamondback-rattlesnake.description: The western diamondback rattlesnake is one of the most dangerous snakes in North America. Found across the southwestern United States and Mexico, it is responsible for the majority of snakebite fatalities in the region. Its rattle serves as a warning when threatened.
western-diamondback-rattlesnake.funFact: Una serpiente de cascabel del oeste

caiman-lizard.name: Caiman Lizard
caiman-lizard.description: The caiman lizard is a semi-aquatic lizard found in the swamps and rivers of South America. It has a flattened tail for swimming and powerful jaws for crushing snail shells. Its skin resembles that of a caiman, hence its name.

carpet-python.name: Carpet Python
carpet-python.description: The carpet python is a large, non-venomous snake found across Australia and New Guinea. It has a variable pattern of dark bands on a lighter background. It is arboreal and commonly found in trees and on the roofs of houses.

brown-basilisk.name: Brown Basilisk
brown-basilisk.description: The brown basilisk is a large lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Central America. It has a distinctive crest on its head and can run bipedally across water. It is semi-arboreal and often found near streams and rivers.

dumerils-boa.name: Dumeril's Boa
dumerils-boa.description: Dumeril's boa is a heavy-bodied, non-venomous snake endemic to Madagascar. It has a tan and brown pattern that provides excellent camouflage on the forest floor. It is a ground-dwelling ambush predator feeding on mammals and birds.

common-caiman.name: Common Caiman
common-caiman.description: The common caiman is a medium-sized crocodilian found throughout Central and South America. It is one of the most widespread crocodilian species. It feeds primarily on fish and invertebrates and is often found in large groups basking on riverbanks.

western-hognose-snake.name: Western Hognose Snake
western-hognose-snake.description: The western hognose snake is a small, non-venomous snake with an upturned snout used for burrowing. Found in the sandy prairies of central North America, it is known for its dramatic threat display. It feeds primarily on toads and small rodents.

forest-cobra.name: Forest Cobra
forest-cobra.description: The forest cobra is the largest cobra species, found in the tropical forests and savannas of central and western Africa. It is highly venomous and can spit venom accurately. It is a strong swimmer and often found near bodies of water.

veiled-chameleon.name: Veiled Chameleon
veiled-chameleon.description: The veiled chameleon is one of the most popular pet chameleon species, native to Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Males have a distinctive tall casque on their heads. It is an arboreal species that feeds on insects by projecting its long, sticky tongue.

rough-scaled-sand-boa.name: Rough-Scaled Sand Boa
rough-scaled-sand-boa.description: The rough-scaled sand boa is a small, non-venomous constrictor found in the arid deserts of South Asia. It has a stout body adapted for burrowing and spends most of its time beneath the sand. It feeds primarily on rodents and small lizards.

philippine-crocodile.name: Philippine Crocodile
philippine-crocodile.description: The Philippine crocodile is a critically endangered species endemic to the Philippines. It is the most endangered crocodilian in the world, with a wild population estimated at fewer than 100 individuals. It inhabits freshwater rivers, lakes, and marshes.
philippine-crocodile.funFact: Un cocodrilo en peligro de Filipinas

rainbow-boa.name: Rainbow Boa
rainbow-boa.description: The rainbow boa is a non-venomous constrictor found in the rainforests of South America. Its name comes from the iridescent sheen of its scales, which refract light to create a rainbow effect. It is a terrestrial species found on the forest floor.

giant-plated-lizard.name: Giant Plated Lizard
giant-plated-lizard.description: The giant plated lizard is a large, robust lizard found in the rocky outcrops of southern and eastern Africa. It has heavy, plate-like scales and a powerful tail. It is semi-arboreal and feeds on insects, small vertebrates, and fruit.

black-spiny-tailed-iguana.name: Black Spiny-Tailed Iguana
black-spiny-tailed-iguana.description: The black spiny-tailed iguana is the fastest lizard in the world, reaching speeds of 21 mph. Native to Central America, it is found on rocky cliffs, walls, and in urban areas. It is an omnivorous species that feeds on plants and small animals.

burmese-python.name: Burmese Python
burmese-python.description: The Burmese python is one of the five largest snakes in the world, native to Southeast Asia. It is a popular pet species but has become a significant invasive species in the Florida Everglades. It is a powerful constrictor that feeds on mammals and birds.

ornate-box-turtle.name: Ornate Box Turtle
ornate-box-turtle.description: The ornate box turtle is a small, terrestrial turtle native to the prairies of central North America. It has a domed shell with intricate yellow and orange patterns. It can fully close its hinged plastron to protect itself from predators.

common-house-gecko.name: Common House Gecko
common-house-gecko.description: The common house gecko is a small, nocturnal lizard found throughout the tropical and subtropical regions of the world. It is commonly seen on walls and ceilings of buildings, hunting insects. Its toe pads allow it to climb smooth vertical surfaces.

sidewinder-rattlesnake.name: Sidewinder Rattlesnake
sidewinder-rattlesnake.description: The sidewinder rattlesnake is a venomous pit viper adapted to desert life in the southwestern United States. It uses a distinctive sidewinding locomotion that leaves J-shaped tracks in the sand. It buries itself in sand to ambush prey and escape heat.
sidewinder-rattlesnake.funFact: Una serpiente que se desplaza lateralmente

chinese-water-dragon.name: Chinese Water Dragon
chinese-water-dragon.description: The Chinese water dragon is an arboreal agamid lizard found near streams in the forests of southeastern China. Males display vibrant green with white and orange markings. It is an excellent swimmer and can hold its breath for up to an hour.

west-african-dwarf-crocodile.name: West African Dwarf Crocodile
west-african-dwarf-crocodile.description: The West African dwarf crocodile is the smallest living crocodile species, found in the swamps and rivers of western and central Africa. It is nocturnal and highly terrestrial, digging burrows for shelter. It feeds primarily on fish, crustaceans, and insects.
west-african-dwarf-crocodile.funFact: Un cocodrilo enano de África occidental

cape-cobra.name: Cape Cobra
cape-cobra.description: The Cape cobra is one of the most dangerous cobras in Africa, found in the shrublands and fynbos of southern Africa. It is highly venomous with potent neurotoxin. It is a diurnal species and an excellent climber.

crested-iguana.name: Crested Iguana
crested-iguana.description: The crested iguana is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry forests of western Madagascar. It has a distinctive high dorsal crest and is one of the rarest iguanas in the world. It is primarily herbivorous, feeding on leaves and fruit.

argentine-tegu.name: Argentine Black and White Tegu
argentine-tegu.description: The Argentine black and white tegu is a large, omnivorous lizard native to South America. It has distinctive black and white banding and a robust body. It feeds on a wide variety of foods including insects, small animals, fruit, and eggs.

king-brown-snake.name: King Brown Snake
king-brown-snake.description: The king brown snake, also known as the mulga snake, is one of Australia's most widespread and dangerous snakes. Despite its name, it belongs to the black snake genus Pseudechis. It is responsible for more snakebite deaths in Australia than any other species.

false-gharial.name: False Gharial
false-gharial.description: The false gharial is a critically endangered crocodilian found in the rivers and swamps of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive long, narrow snout and is one of the largest crocodilian species. It is a specialist fish-eater with a unique jaw structure.

indian-star-tortoise.name: Indian Star Tortoise
indian-star-tortoise.description: The Indian star tortoise is a small to medium-sized tortoise native to India and Sri Lanka. It has distinctive star-shaped patterns on its carapace that radiate from the center of each scute. It is a popular species in the illegal pet trade.
indian-star-tortoise.funFact: Una tortuga estrellada de la India

green-anaconda.name: Green Anaconda
green-anaconda.description: The green anaconda is the heaviest and one of the longest snakes in the world, found in the swamps and rivers of South America. It is a non-venomous constrictor that feeds on deer, capybaras, and even jaguars. It spends most of its time in water.
green-anaconda.funFact: La serpiente más pesada del mundo

tuatara.name: Tuatara
tuatara.description: The tuatara is a reptile endemic to New Zealand and the only surviving member of the order Rhynchocephalia. Often called a living fossil, it has remained virtually unchanged for 200 million years. It has a third eye on top of its head that detects light changes.
tuatara.funFact: Un reptil primitivo de Nueva Zelanda

eastern-water-dragon.name: Eastern Water Dragon
eastern-water-dragon.description: The eastern water dragon is a large agamid lizard found along rivers and creeks in eastern Australia. Males have a distinctive red chest and a spiny crest along their back. It is semi-aquatic and an excellent swimmer.

spider-tortoise.name: Spider Tortoise
spider-tortoise.description: The spider tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry spiny forests of southern Madagascar. It has distinctive yellow radiating patterns on its dark shell that resemble a spider's web. It is one of the smallest tortoise species in the world.
spider-tortoise.funFact: Una tortuga de patrón de araña

russian-tortoise.name: Russian Tortoise
russian-tortoise.description: The Russian tortoise is a small species native to the arid steppes of Central Asia. It is one of the most cold-tolerant tortoise species, surviving harsh winters by brumating underground. It is popular in the pet trade due to its small size and hardy nature.

cat-eyed-snake.name: Cat-Eyed Snake
cat-eyed-snake.description: The cat-eyed snake is a small, rear-fanged snake found in the tropical rainforests of Central and South America. It has distinctive vertical pupils and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on frogs, lizards, and small mammals.
cat-eyed-snake.funFact: Una serpiente de ojos de gato

arabian-chameleon.name: Arabian Chameleon
arabian-chameleon.description: The Arabian chameleon is a species of chameleon native to the Arabian Peninsula. It is adapted to arid conditions, unlike most chameleon species. It has a casque on its head and can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

spotted-turtle.name: Spotted Turtle
spotted-turtle.description: The spotted turtle is one of the smallest turtles in North America, found in shallow, slow-moving waters. It has a smooth, dark shell with distinctive yellow or orange spots. It is a long-lived species that can survive for over a century.

banded-krait.name: Banded Krait
banded-krait.description: The banded krait is a highly venomous elapid found in South and Southeast Asia. It has distinctive black and yellow bands and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on other snakes, including venomous species, and is responsible for many snakebite deaths in Asia.

golden-skink.name: Golden Skink
golden-skink.description: The golden skink is a small, fast-moving lizard found in tropical forests and gardens across South and Southeast Asia. It has a metallic, iridescent body that gives it a golden appearance. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

broad-snouted-caiman.name: Broad-Snouted Caiman
broad-snouted-caiman.description: The broad-snouted caiman is a medium-sized crocodilian found in the freshwater habitats of South America. It has a broad, flat snout adapted for catching fish and invertebrates. It builds vegetation mounds to incubate its eggs.

copperhead.name: Copperhead
copperhead.description: The copperhead is a venomous pit viper found across the eastern United States. It has a distinctive copper-colored head and hourglass-shaped crossbands. It is responsible for the most snakebite cases in North America, though fatalities are rare.

radiated-tortoise.name: Radiated Tortoise
radiated-tortoise.description: The radiated tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to Madagascar. It has a high-domed shell with striking yellow star-shaped patterns radiating from the center of each scute. It is threatened by habitat loss and poaching for food and the pet trade.

blue-racer.name: Blue Racer
blue-racer.description: The blue racer is a fast-moving, non-venomous colubrid found across the central United States and southern Ontario. It has a distinctive blue-grey dorsal color and a white or cream underside. It is diurnal and feeds on rodents, frogs, and other snakes.

side-blotched-lizard.name: Side-Blotched Lizard
side-blotched-lizard.description: The side-blotched lizard is a small lizard found in the deserts and grasslands of western North America. It is famous in evolutionary biology for its rock-paper-scissors mating strategy. Males have three throat colors that correspond to different mating tactics.

nile-monitor.name: Nile Monitor
nile-monitor.description: The Nile monitor is a large, powerful lizard found throughout sub-Saharan Africa near water. It is semi-aquatic and feeds on fish, frogs, birds, eggs, and carrion. It has a forked tongue used for detecting prey in the water.

canebrake-rattlesnake.name: Canebrake Rattlesnake
canebrake-rattlesnake.description: The canebrake rattlesnake, a subspecies of the timber rattlesnake, is found in the forests and swamps of the southeastern United States. It has a distinctive pinkish-brown color with dark crossbands. It is a dangerous venomous pit viper.
canebrake-rattlesnake.funFact: Una serpiente de cascabel de cañaveral

yellow-footed-tortoise.name: Yellow-Footed Tortoise
yellow-footed-tortoise.description: The yellow-footed tortoise is a medium-sized tortoise native to the Amazon Basin of South America. It has distinctive yellow or orange scales on its legs and head. It feeds primarily on fallen fruit and plays an important ecological role in seed dispersal.

puff-adder.name: Puff Adder
puff-adder.description: The puff adder is a venomous viper found throughout sub-Saharan Africa. It relies on its excellent camouflage and will not flee when approached, leading to many defensive strikes. It is an ambush predator that strikes with incredible speed.

eastern-green-mamba.name: Eastern Green Mamba
eastern-green-mamba.description: The eastern green mamba is a fast, highly venomous elapid found in the coastal forests of eastern and southern Africa. It is bright green, blending perfectly with the forest canopy. Unlike the black mamba, it is arboreal and rarely comes to the ground.

cape-dwarf-chameleon.name: Cape Dwarf Chameleon
cape-dwarf-chameleon.description: The Cape dwarf chameleon is a small chameleon endemic to the Western Cape of South Africa. It has independently rotating eyes, a prehensile tail, and a long, sticky tongue for catching insects. It can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

chinese-alligator.name: Chinese Alligator
chinese-alligator.description: The Chinese alligator is a critically endangered species, one of only two alligator species in the world. Found in eastern China, it is smaller than the American alligator and has bony plates on its eyelids. Wild populations are critically low.
chinese-alligator.funFact: Un aligátor en peligro de China

snouted-cobra.name: Snouted Cobra
snouted-cobra.description: The snouted cobra is a large, highly venomous snake found across southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned snout and can spit venom accurately. It is found in a wide variety of habitats and feeds on rodents, birds, and other snakes.

common-wall-lizard.name: Common Wall Lizard
common-wall-lizard.description: The common wall lizard is a small, agile lizard found across Europe and introduced to North America. It is commonly seen basking on stone walls and buildings. It feeds on insects, spiders, and small invertebrates.

brown-tree-snake.name: Brown Tree Snake
brown-tree-snake.description: The brown tree snake is an arboreal, rear-fanged snake native to Australia and New Guinea. It has become one of the world's most destructive invasive species on Guam, where it has eliminated most of the island's native bird species. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds, lizards, and mammals.

angulate-tortoise.name: Angulate Tortoise
angulate-tortoise.description: The angulate tortoise is a small tortoise found in the fynbos and karoo shrublands of southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned front margin to its shell. It is well adapted to the Mediterranean climate of the Western Cape region.

savannah-monitor.name: Savannah Monitor
savannah-monitor.description: The savannah monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found across sub-Saharan Africa. It is a ground-dwelling species that digs burrows for shelter. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and reptiles, and is popular in the exotic pet trade.

white-lipped-pit-viper.name: White-Lipped Pit Viper
white-lipped-pit-viper.description: The white-lipped pit viper is a venomous snake found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive white or yellow line along its upper lip and is primarily arboreal. It is a nocturnal ambush predator that feeds on rodents and birds.
white-lipped-pit-viper.funFact: Una víbora de fosa de labios blancos

alabama-red-bellied-cooter.name: Alabama Red-Bellied Cooter
alabama-red-bellied-cooter.description: The Alabama red-bellied cooter is an endangered freshwater turtle endemic to Alabama and Georgia. It has a dark shell with a distinctive red or orange plastron. It is found in rivers, lakes, and ponds with abundant aquatic vegetation.
alabama-red-bellied-cooter.funFact: Una tortuga de vientre rojo en peligro

amazon-tree-boa.name: Amazon Tree Boa
amazon-tree-boa.description: The Amazon tree boa is a small, arboreal constrictor found throughout the Amazon rainforest. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds and small mammals. It has an extremely variable color pattern, ranging from yellow to red to brown.

california-kingsnake.name: California Kingsnake
california-kingsnake.description: The California kingsnake is a popular, non-venomous constrictor found across the western United States. It has a banded pattern of brown and white or yellow. It is an opportunistic feeder that readily eats rattlesnakes, making it beneficial to humans.

clouded-monitor.name: Clouded Monitor
clouded-monitor.description: The clouded monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It is arboreal and has a long, slender body adapted for climbing. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and birds.

brazilian-rainbow-boa.name: Brazilian Rainbow Boa
brazilian-rainbow-boa.description: The Brazilian rainbow boa is a medium-sized, non-venomous constrictor found in the rainforests of South America. Its name comes from the stunning iridescent sheen of its scales. It is primarily terrestrial and feeds on rodents, birds, and bats.

northern-cuirassated-lizard.name: Northern Cuirassated Lizard
northern-cuirassated-lizard.description: The northern cuirassated lizard is a small lizard found in the rocky hillsides of Mexico. It has distinctive bony armor plates called osteoderms covering its body. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

desert-iguana.name: Desert Iguana
desert-iguana.description: The desert iguana is a medium-sized lizard found in the deserts of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It is one of the most heat-tolerant lizards, active at temperatures that force other reptiles to seek shade. It feeds primarily on leaves and flowers.

false-water-cobra.name: False Water Cobra
false-water-cobra.description: The false water cobra is a large, semi-aquatic colubrid found in the wetlands of South America. It displays a cobra-like hood when threatened, despite being only mildly venomous. It is an excellent swimmer and feeds on fish, frogs, and small mammals.

garter-snake.name: Common Garter Snake
garter-snake.description: The common garter snake is one of the most widespread snakes in North America, found in gardens, meadows, and woodlands. It has distinctive longitudinal stripes. Despite being mildly venomous, it is harmless to humans and beneficial as pest control.

shingleback-skink.name: Shingleback Skink
shingleback-skink.description: The shingleback skink is a large, slow-moving lizard found in the woodlands and grasslands of southern Australia. It has rough, pinecone-like scales and a short, fat tail that resembles its head, confusing predators. It is one of the few reptile species that mate for life.

mozambique-spitting-cobra.name: Mozambique Spitting Cobra
mozambique-spitting-cobra.description: The Mozambique spitting cobra is a highly venomous elapid found across eastern and southern Africa. It is one of the most dangerous snakes in the region, responsible for many snakebite cases. It can spit venom accurately into the eyes of perceived threats.

glass-frog.name: Glass Frog
glass-frog.description: Glass Frogs are remarkable amphibians with translucent ventral skin. Found in Central and South America, they spend most of their lives in trees and descend only to breed near fast-flowing streams.

pacman-frog.name: Pacman Frog
pacman-frog.description: The Pacman Frog, also known as the Argentine Horned Frog, is a popular pet species known for its large mouth and sedentary lifestyle. They are ambush predators that sit and wait for prey to pass by.

budgetts-frog.name: Budgett's Frog
budgetts-frog.description: Budgett's Frog is a flattened, broad-bodied frog found in South America. They are known for their aggressive defensive behavior, including inflating, screaming, and biting when disturbed.

whites-tree-frog.name: White's Tree Frog
whites-tree-frog.description: White's Tree Frog, also known as the Dumpy Tree Frog, is one of the most docile and popular amphibian pets. Native to Australia and New Guinea, they are known for their placid temperament and ability to thrive in captivity.

african-dwarf-frog.name: African Dwarf Frog
african-dwarf-frog.description: African Dwarf Frogs are tiny, fully aquatic amphibians that never leave the water. They are social creatures that do best in groups and are popular aquarium pets due to their small size and active nature.

amazon-milk-frog.name: Amazon Milk Frog
amazon-milk-frog.description: The Amazon Milk Frog is a large tree frog found in the Amazon rainforest. They have a distinctive black and white or blue and white banded pattern and are named for the milky toxic substance they secrete.

gray-tree-frog.name: Gray Tree Frog
gray-tree-frog.description: The Gray Tree Frog is a small, arboreal frog native to eastern North America. They have bumpy skin that resembles tree bark and bright yellow-orange patches on the inside of their hind legs.

spring-peeper.name: Spring Peeper
spring-peeper.description: Spring Peepers are tiny tree frogs whose chorus marks the arrival of spring in eastern North America. Their characteristic X-shaped marking on their back helps identify them among other small frogs.
spring-peeper.funFact: Una rana que anuncia la primavera

wood-frog.name: Wood Frog
wood-frog.description: Wood Frogs are remarkable for their ability to freeze during winter and thaw out alive in spring. Found across North America, they have a distinctive dark mask marking behind each eye.
wood-frog.funFact: Una rana que tolera la congelación

american-toad.name: American Toad
american-toad.description: The American Toad is one of the most common and widespread toads in North America. They have warty skin, parotoid glands that produce a mild toxin, and can live for over a decade in the wild.

cane-toad.name: Cane Toad
cane-toad.description: The Cane Toad is a large, toxic toad native to Central and South America. It has become one of the most successful invasive amphibians, spreading across Australia, the Caribbean, and Pacific islands.

fire-bellied-toad.name: Fire-Bellied Toad
fire-bellied-toad.description: Fire-Bellied Toads are small, semi-aquatic toads with bumpy olive-green backs and vivid orange or red bellies. They are popular pets and are known for their aposematic coloration that warns predators of their toxins.
fire-bellied-toad.funFact: Un sapo de vientre de fuego

desert-rain-frog.name: Desert Rain Frog
desert-rain-frog.description: The Desert Rain Frog is a tiny, round frog that burrows into sand along the coast of South Africa and Namibia. They spend most of their lives underground and emerge only to feed and breed during foggy conditions.
desert-rain-frog.funFact: El sapo más adorable del desierto

goliath-frog.name: Goliath Frog
goliath-frog.description: The Goliath Frog, or Conraua goliath, is the world's largest frog. Found only in Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea, these massive amphibians inhabit fast-flowing rivers and are threatened by habitat loss and hunting.
goliath-frog.funFact: La rana más grande del mundo

mountain-chicken-frog.name: Mountain Chicken Frog
mountain-chicken-frog.description: The Mountain Chicken Frog is one of the largest frogs in the Caribbean, found only on Dominica and Montserrat. They are critically endangered due to the chytrid fungus and habitat destruction.

spadefoot-toad.name: Spadefoot Toad
spadefoot-toad.description: Spadefoot Toads are adapted to arid environments with specialized keratinized spades on their hind feet for burrowing. They spend most of their lives underground and breed explosively in temporary rain pools.

natterjack-toad.name: Natterjack Toad
natterjack-toad.description: The Natterjack Toad is a medium-sized toad found across Europe. Unlike most toads, they run rather than hop and are known for their loud, rasping calls during breeding season.

midwife-toad.name: Midwife Toad
midwife-toad.description: Midwife Toads are small, nocturnal toads named for the male's paternal behavior of carrying eggs on his hind legs. Found across Europe, they have a distinctive high-pitched beep-like call.
midwife-toad.funFact: Un sapo que lleva huevos en las patas

european-tree-frog.name: European Tree Frog
european-tree-frog.description: The European Tree Frog is a small, bright green frog with a distinctive dark stripe along each side. They are excellent climbers and are often found in gardens, orchards, and damp woodlands.

leopard-frog.name: Leopard Frog
leopard-frog.description: The Leopard Frog gets its name from the distinctive dark spots covering its green or brown body. Found across North America, they are strong jumpers and swimmers that inhabit a variety of wetland habitats.

strawberry-poison-dart-frog.name: Strawberry Poison Dart Frog
strawberry-poison-dart-frog.description: The Strawberry Poison Dart Frog, also known as the Blue Jeans Frog, is a small but vividly colored amphibian found in Central America. Males carry tadpoles on their backs to suitable pools of water.

dyeing-poison-dart-frog.name: Dyeing Poison Dart Frog
dyeing-poison-dart-frog.description: The Dyeing Poison Dart Frog is a variable species with striking color patterns. Found in South America, they were named for the use of their skin secretions by indigenous peoples to dye feathers and textiles.

harlequin-toad.name: Harlequin Toad
harlequin-toad.description: Harlequin Toads are a diverse group of brightly colored toads found in Central and South America. Many species are critically endangered or believed extinct due to the chytrid fungus and habitat loss.

pickerel-frog.name: Pickerel Frog
pickerel-frog.description: The Pickerel Frog is a brownish frog with two parallel rows of dark rectangular spots down its back. Found in eastern North America, they are one of the few frogs whose skin secretions are toxic to other amphibians.

cherry-tree-frog.name: Cherry Tree Frog
cherry-tree-frog.description: The Cherry Tree Frog is a small European tree frog known for its distinctive call that sounds like a cherry pit being clicked. They are excellent climbers with adhesive toe pads.

asian-common-toad.name: Asian Common Toad
asian-common-toad.description: The Asian Common Toad is a widespread toad found across South and Southeast Asia. They are highly adaptable to urban environments and are often found in gardens, drains, and agricultural areas.

clown-tree-frog.name: Clown Tree Frog
clown-tree-frog.description: The Clown Tree Frog is a colorful, medium-sized tree frog found in the Amazon rainforest. They have striking patterns of brown, green, and cream that provide excellent camouflage against tree bark.

gliding-tree-frog.name: Gliding Tree Frog
gliding-tree-frog.description: The Gliding Tree Frog has evolved enlarged adhesive toe pads and partially webbed feet that allow it to glide through the rainforest canopy. Found in Central America, they are active at night.

black-legged-poison-frog.name: Black-Legged Poison Frog
black-legged-poison-frog.description: The Black-Legged Poison Frog is a small, toxic frog found in the rainforests of Colombia. They are known for their complex parental care behaviors and striking black and yellow coloration.
black-legged-poison-frog.funFact: Una rana venenosa de patas negras

red-backed-poison-frog.name: Red-Backed Poison Frog
red-backed-poison-frog.description: The Red-Backed Poison Frog is a small, brightly colored amphibian found in the Amazon rainforest. Their vivid red or orange back serves as a warning to potential predators.
red-backed-poison-frog.funFact: Una rana venenosa de espalda roja

splashback-poison-frog.name: Splashback Poison Frog
splashback-poison-frog.description: The Splashback Poison Frog is a small amphibian with vivid coloration that varies from green to blue to yellow. Found in South America, they carry tadpoles on their backs to water-filled bromeliads.

cane-turtle-frog.name: Cane Turtle Frog
cane-turtle-frog.description: The Cane Turtle Frog is a small, flattened frog found in South America. They are often found in agricultural areas, particularly sugarcane fields, and have a distinctive flattened appearance.

malaysian-horned-frog.name: Malaysian Horned Frog
malaysian-horned-frog.description: The Malaysian Horned Frog is a medium-sized frog with distinctive horn-like projections above each eye. Found in Southeast Asian rainforests, they are well-camouflaged among dead leaves on the forest floor.

hampire-poison-dart-frog.name: Hampire Poison Dart Frog
hampire-poison-dart-frog.description: The Hamphire Poison Dart Frog is a small, strikingly colored amphibian found in South America. Their bold pattern serves as a warning to predators of their toxic skin secretions.

brazilian-horned-frog.name: Brazilian Horned Frog
brazilian-horned-frog.description: The Brazilian Horned Frog is a medium-sized frog with horn-like projections above its eyes. Found in the Amazon rainforest, they are well-camouflaged and lie in wait to ambush passing prey.

hairy-frog.name: Hairy Frog
hairy-frog.description: The Hairy Frog, also known as the Trichobatrachus, is a unique amphibian found in Central Africa. Males develop hair-like dermal papillae on their flanks and thighs during the breeding season.

tomato-frog.name: Tomato Frog
tomato-frog.description: The Tomato Frog is a bright red-orange frog found in Madagascar. When threatened, they inflate their bodies and secrete a sticky white substance that can temporarily immobilize predators.

marsupial-frog.name: Marsupial Frog
marsupial-frog.description: The Marsupial Frog is a remarkable amphibian found in the Andes mountains. Females have a dorsal pouch where they carry their eggs until they develop into froglets, bypassing the tadpole stage.

foam-nest-frog.name: Foam Nest Frog
foam-nest-frog.description: Foam Nest Frogs are found across Africa and South America. They are named for their unique breeding behavior where both sexes whip up a foam nest to protect their eggs from drying out.
foam-nest-frog.funFact: Una rana de nido de espuma

surinam-toad.name: Surinam Toad
surinam-toad.description: The Surinam Toad is a flat, bottom-dwelling amphibian found in South America. Females have a remarkable reproductive strategy where eggs are embedded in the skin of their backs until they emerge as fully formed froglets.

tiger-salamander.name: Tiger Salamander
tiger-salamander.description: The Tiger Salamander is the largest terrestrial salamander in North America. They have distinctive yellow or olive markings on a dark background and spend most of their lives underground in burrows.

eastern-newt.name: Eastern Newt
eastern-newt.description: The Eastern Newt has a complex life cycle with three distinct stages: aquatic larva, terrestrial red eft, and aquatic adult. Found in eastern North America, they produce tetrodotoxin in their skin.

hellbender.name: Hellbender
hellbender.description: The Hellbender is the largest salamander in North America, reaching up to two feet long. Found in clean, fast-flowing streams of the eastern United States, they are declining due to pollution and habitat loss.

olm.name: Olm
olm.description: The Olm is a blind, cave-dwelling salamander found in the caves of southern Europe. It has no eyes, is depigmented, and can live for over 100 years, making it one of the longest-lived vertebrates.

fire-salamander.name: Fire Salamander
fire-salamander.description: The Fire Salamander is one of Europe's most recognizable amphibians with its striking black body and bright yellow or orange markings. Found in central and southern Europe, they secrete samandarin, a neurotoxin.

spotted-salamander.name: Spotted Salamander
spotted-salamander.description: The Spotted Salamander is a large, robust salamander found in eastern North America. They have distinctive yellow spots on a dark background and are one of the few vertebrates known to have algae living inside their cells.

red-backed-salamander.name: Red-Backed Salamander
red-backed-salamander.description: The Red-Backed Salamander is the most common and abundant salamander in eastern North America. They are entirely lungless, breathing through their moist skin, and come in both red-backed and lead-backed color phases.

mudpuppy.name: Mudpuppy
mudpuppy.description: The Mudpuppy is a fully aquatic salamander found in eastern North America. They retain their bushy red external gills throughout life and are nocturnal hunters that use sensory barbels to find prey.

rough-skinned-newt.name: Rough-Skinned Newt
rough-skinned-newt.description: The Rough-Skinned Newt is a highly toxic amphibian found along the Pacific coast of North America. They produce tetrodotoxin, the same toxin found in pufferfish, and advertise their toxicity with bright orange undersides.

alpine-salamander.name: Alpine Salamander
alpine-salamander.description: The Alpine Salamander is found in the mountains of central and southern Europe. Unlike most amphibians, they give birth to live young that have completed their development inside the mother's body.

great-crested-newt.name: Great Crested Newt
great-crested-newt.description: The Great Crested Newt is the largest newt species in Europe. Males develop a distinctive crest during breeding season and have a white flash on their tail. They are legally protected in many countries.

marbled-salamander.name: Marbled Salamander
marbled-salamander.description: The Marbled Salamander is a small, stocky salamander with distinctive white or gray crossbands on a dark background. Found in eastern North America, they are one of the few salamanders that guard their eggs.

long-toed-salamander.name: Long-Toed Salamander
long-toed-salamander.description: The Long-Toed Salamander is a small salamander found across western North America. They have a characteristic stripe running down their back and long toes that give them their name.

slimy-salamander.name: Slimy Salamander
slimy-salamander.description: The Slimy Salamander is a medium-sized lungless salamander found in the eastern United States. They secrete a sticky white substance from their skin that helps deter predators.

red-salamander.name: Red Salamander
red-salamander.description: The Red Salamander is a brightly colored amphibian found in the Appalachian region of the eastern United States. Adults have a distinctive red to orange coloration with scattered black spots.

lesser-siren.name: Lesser Siren
lesser-siren.description: The Lesser Siren is a fully aquatic salamander with external gills found in the southeastern United States. They lack hind legs and can survive drought by burrowing into mud and entering a dormant state.

greater-siren.name: Greater Siren
greater-siren.description: The Greater Siren is a large, fully aquatic salamander with external gills found in the coastal plains of the southeastern United States. They lack hind limbs and can grow up to three feet long.

three-toed-amphiuma.name: Three-Toed Amphiuma
three-toed-amphiuma.description: The Three-Toed Amphiuma is a fully aquatic salamander found in the southeastern United States. It has an eel-like body with three tiny, non-functional toes on each vestigial limb.

waterdog.name: Waterdog
waterdog.description: The Waterdog is a fully aquatic salamander found in eastern North America. Like the mudpuppy, it retains its external gills throughout life and is an important indicator of stream health.

spring-salamander.name: Spring Salamander
spring-salamander.description: The Spring Salamander is a large, robust salamander found in cold mountain streams of eastern North America. They have a distinctive salmon or orange coloration with dark reticulations.

cave-salamander.name: Cave Salamander
cave-salamander.description: The Cave Salamander is a brightly colored salamander with orange to red body and black spots. Found in caves and rocky areas of the eastern United States, they are excellent climbers.

arboreal-salamander.name: Arboreal Salamander
arboreal-salamander.description: The Arboreal Salamander is a lungless salamander found in the coastal mountains of California. They are excellent climbers, spending much of their time in oak trees and rock crevices.

ensatina.name: Ensatina
ensatina.description: The Ensatina is a colorful salamander found along the Pacific coast of North America. They are famous in evolutionary biology as an example of a ring species, with different color morphs forming a circle around California's Central Valley.

slender-salamander.name: Slender Salamander
slender-salamander.description: The Slender Salamander is a small, lungless salamander found in California. They have long, thin bodies and can coil into a spiral when disturbed or to prevent water loss.

ringed-salamander.name: Ringed Salamander
ringed-salamander.description: The Ringed Salamander is a large, dark salamander with yellow or white rings or spots. Found in the Ozark Plateau region of the United States, they are one of the few salamanders that breed in the fall.

flatwoods-salamander.name: Flatwoods Salamander
flatwoods-salamander.description: The Flatwoods Salamander is a small, threatened salamander found in the longleaf pine forests of the southeastern United States. They breed in temporary fishless ponds and are declining due to habitat loss.

dusky-salamander.name: Dusky Salamander
dusky-salamander.description: The Dusky Salamander is a medium-sized lungless salamander found in eastern North America. They are variable in color and pattern and are often found near streams and springs.

four-toed-salamander.name: Four-Toed Salamander
four-toed-salamander.description: The Four-Toed Salamander is a small salamander found in bogs and wetlands of eastern North America. They are the only salamander in their range with four toes on their hind feet.

gulf-coast-salamander.name: Gulf Coast Salamander
gulf-coast-salamander.description: The Gulf Coast Salamander is a small salamander found in the coastal lowlands of the southeastern United States. They are often found in bottomland hardwood forests and can tolerate mildly saline conditions.
gulf-coast-salamander.funFact: Una salamandra de la costa del Golfo

tropical-caecilian.name: Tropical Caecilian
tropical-caecilian.description: Tropical Caecilians are limbless, serpentine amphibians found in tropical regions of the world. They live underground or in leaf litter, feeding on small invertebrates, and are the least known order of amphibians.

boulengers-caecilian.name: Boulenger's Caecilian
boulengers-caecilian.description: Boulenger's Caecilian is one of the largest caecilian species, found in South America. These burrowing amphibians have ring-like grooves along their body and tiny, non-functional eyes buried beneath the skin.

ringed-caecilian.name: Ringed Caecilian
ringed-caecilian.description: The Ringed Caecilian is a limbless amphibian found in South America and the Caribbean. They have a distinctive ring-like pattern on their body and use a chemosensory tentacle to find prey in the soil.

luna-moth.name: Luna Moth
luna-moth.description: The luna moth is a large, pale green moth with long tail-like hindwings. It is nocturnal and attracted to light, and adults do not feed, dedicating their brief adult lives entirely to reproduction.

atlas-moth.name: Atlas Moth
atlas-moth.description: The atlas moth is the largest moth species, with a wingspan that can exceed 12 inches. Its wings have snake-head-shaped tips that deter predators, and like other giant moths, adults do not feed.
atlas-moth.funFact: La polilla más grande del mundo

swallowtail-butterfly.name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail
swallowtail-butterfly.description: The eastern tiger swallowtail is a large, bright yellow butterfly with distinctive black tiger stripes. It is one of the most common and recognizable butterflies in eastern North America.

hawk-moth.name: Hawk Moth
hawk-moth.description: Hawk moths, also known as sphinx moths, are powerful fliers with streamlined bodies. Many species have extremely long proboscises for feeding on deep-throated flowers while hovering.

painted-lady-butterfly.name: Painted Lady Butterfly
painted-lady-butterfly.description: The painted lady is one of the most widespread butterflies on Earth, found on every continent except Antarctica. It is a strong migrant and a common visitor to gardens.

blue-morpho-butterfly.name: Blue Morpho Butterfly
blue-morpho-butterfly.description: The blue morpho is a brilliantly iridescent blue butterfly found in tropical rainforests. Its metallic blue wings are visible from great distances and are produced by light diffraction rather than pigment.

glasswing-butterfly.name: Glasswing Butterfly
glasswing-butterfly.description: The glasswing butterfly has remarkably transparent wings with only a thin dark border. The transparency is caused by tiny nanopillar structures on the wings that prevent light reflection.

cecropia-moth.name: Cecropia Moth
cecropia-moth.description: The cecropia moth is North America's largest moth with wingspans reaching 7 inches. It has striking red, orange, and white markings and, like other giant moths, adults do not feed.
cecropia-moth.funFact: La polilla más grande de Norteamérica

io-moth.name: Io Moth
io-moth.description: The io moth is a beautiful silk moth with large eyespots on each wing. Males are yellow while females are reddish-brown, and both sexes flash their eyespots when threatened.

polyphemus-moth.name: Polyphemus Moth
polyphemus-moth.description: The polyphemus moth is a large, tan-colored silk moth with distinctive eyespots on its hindwings. It is named after the Cyclops of Greek mythology due to the large eyespots.
polyphemus-moth.funFact: Una polilla con ojos en las alas

viceroy-butterfly.name: Viceroy Butterfly
viceroy-butterfly.description: The viceroy butterfly closely resembles the monarch and was long thought to be a mimic. It is now known to be somewhat distasteful to predators, making it a Müllerian mimic.
viceroy-butterfly.funFact: Una mariposa que imita a la monarca

red-admiral-butterfly.name: Red Admiral Butterfly
red-admiral-butterfly.description: The red admiral is a striking black butterfly with bold red-orange bands and white spots. It is a strong flier found worldwide and often visits rotting fruit and tree sap.

great-spangled-fritillary.name: Great Spangled Fritillary
great-spangled-fritillary.description: The great spangled fritillary is a large, orange butterfly with distinctive silver-spotted underwings. Its larvae feed on various violet species while adults nectar on milkweed and coneflowers.

clouded-yellow-butterfly.name: Clouded Yellow
clouded-yellow-butterfly.description: The clouded yellow is a bright golden butterfly common across Europe and parts of Asia. It is a strong migratory species that sometimes appears in large numbers in areas outside its normal range.

comma-butterfly.name: Comma Butterfly
comma-butterfly.description: The comma butterfly has uniquely ragged wing edges that help camouflage it as a dead leaf. It has a distinctive white comma-shaped mark on its dark brown underwings.
comma-butterfly.funFact: Una mariposa con marca de coma

mourning-cloak-butterfly.name: Mourning Cloak Butterfly
mourning-cloak-butterfly.description: The mourning cloak is one of the longest-lived butterflies, surviving up to 11 months. It overwinters as an adult and is often the first butterfly seen in spring, with dark wings bordered in yellow.
mourning-cloak-butterfly.funFact: Una mariposa de manto de luto

zebra-longwing-butterfly.name: Zebra Longwing Butterfly
zebra-longwing-butterfly.description: The zebra longwing is a distinctive butterfly with black wings marked by pale yellow stripes. It is unique among butterflies in that adults can digest pollen, extending their lifespan significantly.
zebra-longwing-butterfly.funFact: Una mariposa de rayas de cebra

snowflake-butterfly.name: Snowflake Butterfly
snowflake-butterfly.description: The snowflake butterfly is a delicate white butterfly found in tropical forests. Its mostly white wings with small dark tips give it a graceful appearance as it glides through forest understory.

resurrection-butterfly.name: Resurrection Butterfly
resurrection-butterfly.description: The resurrection butterfly, known as Kuroneko Yamane in Japan, is a medium-sized butterfly with distinctive markings. It has deep cultural significance in Japan as a symbol of love and resurrection.

cabbage-white-butterfly.name: Small White Butterfly
cabbage-white-butterfly.description: The small white butterfly is a widespread species often found in gardens and agricultural areas. Its caterpillars are major pests of cabbage and other brassica crops.

atlas-beetle.name: Atlas Beetle
atlas-beetle.description: The atlas beetle is a large rhinoceros beetle native to Southeast Asian rainforests. Males have three prominent horns used in combat for mates, and they are among the strongest insects relative to size.

goliath-beetle.name: Goliath Beetle
goliath-beetle.description: The goliath beetle is one of the largest and heaviest insects on Earth, found in African tropical forests. They feed on fruit and tree sap, and their larvae are among the heaviest grubs known.
goliath-beetle.funFact: El escarabajo más pesado del mundo

rhinoceros-beetle.name: Western Hercules Beetle
rhinoceros-beetle.description: The western hercules beetle is a large rhinoceros beetle found in the hardwood forests of North America. Males have a distinctive horn used for wrestling other males during mating season.

stag-beetle.name: Stag Beetle
stag-beetle.description: Stag beetles are named for the large, antler-like mandibles of the males. They spend most of their lives as larvae feeding on decaying wood underground before emerging as impressive adults.

dung-beetle.name: Scarab Dung Beetle
dung-beetle.description: Dung beetles roll animal droppings into balls for food or breeding. They are essential decomposers that help recycle nutrients back into the soil and reduce parasite populations in pastures.

tiger-beetle.name: Six-Spotted Tiger Beetle
tiger-beetle.description: Tiger beetles are fast-running predatory beetles with large eyes and powerful jaws. They are voracious hunters of smaller insects and are often found on open, sunlit ground.

longhorn-beetle.name: Asian Longhorned Beetle
longhorn-beetle.description: The Asian longhorned beetle is an invasive species that attacks a wide variety of hardwood trees. It has distinctive black and white markings and very long antennae that exceed its body length.

click-beetle.name: Click Beetle
click-beetle.description: Click beetles have a unique clicking mechanism on their thorax that allows them to snap and launch into the air when overturned. Their larvae, called wireworms, are important soil dwellers.

bombardier-beetle.name: Bombardier Beetle
bombardier-beetle.description: The bombardier beetle defends itself by ejecting a hot, noxious chemical spray from its abdomen with an audible pop. The spray reaches temperatures near boiling and repels predators effectively.

june-bug.name: June Bug
june-bug.description: June bugs are chunky, brown beetles that emerge in late spring. They are attracted to lights at night and their larvae, known as white grubs, feed on grass roots and can damage lawns.

whirligig-beetle.name: Whirligig Beetle
whirligig-beetle.description: Whirligig beetles are aquatic beetles that spin rapidly on the surface of calm water. They have split eyes adapted for both aerial and aquatic vision and are social insects that form groups.

diving-beetle.name: Predaceous Diving Beetle
diving-beetle.description: Predaceous diving beetles are streamlined aquatic predators that hunt tadpoles, small fish, and other insects underwater. They trap air beneath their elytra for extended submerged hunting.

oil-beetle.name: Oil Beetle
oil-beetle.description: Oil beetles are flightless blister beetles that produce cantharidin, a toxic oily substance, from their joints. Their larvae parasitize solitary bees and develop inside their nests.

bess-beetle.name: Bess Beetle
bess-beetle.description: Bess beetles are large, shiny black beetles that live in decaying wood. They exhibit parental care, with adults feeding and caring for their larvae, which is unusual for beetles.

bark-beetle.name: Mountain Pine Beetle
bark-beetle.description: Mountain pine beetles are tiny bark beetles that bore into pine trees and introduce blue-stain fungi. Massive outbreaks have devastated millions of acres of forest in western North America.

sacred-scarab-beetle.name: Sacred Scarab Beetle
sacred-scarab-beetle.description: The sacred scarab beetle rolls dung into balls and was revered in ancient Egyptian culture as a symbol of rebirth and the sun's daily journey across the sky.

carrion-beetle.name: American Carrion Beetle
carrion-beetle.description: The American carrion beetle is a large, flat beetle that feeds on dead animals and snails. It plays an important ecological role in recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

patrol-bess-beetle.name: Patrol Bess Beetle
patrol-bess-beetle.description: The patrol bess beetle is a large, glossy black beetle found in tropical rainforests. Like other passalid beetles, both parents work together to feed and care for their larvae.

eyed-click-beetle.name: Eyed Click Beetle
eyed-click-beetle.description: The eyed click beetle is a large click beetle with distinctive eyespots on its pronotum. When threatened, it clicks and flips into the air to right itself or escape danger.

rose-chafer.name: Rose Chafer
rose-chafer.description: The rose chafer is a metallic green beetle that feeds on flowers, especially roses and fruit blossoms. Despite being considered a pest, its larvae help decompose organic matter in soil.

japanese-beetle.name: Japanese Beetle
japanese-beetle.description: The Japanese beetle is a highly invasive pest that skeletonizes leaves and damages turf with its white grub larvae. It is native to Japan and has become a devastating pest in North America.

colorado-potato-beetle.name: Colorado Potato Beetle
colorado-potato-beetle.description: The Colorado potato beetle is a major agricultural pest that feeds on potatoes, tomatoes, and eggplants. It has developed resistance to over 50 different insecticides.

lily-beetle.name: Scarlet Lily Beetle
lily-beetle.description: The scarlet lily beetle is a bright red pest of lily plants. Both adults and larvae feed on leaves, stems, and flowers, and the larvae cover themselves in their own excrement for protection.

elm-beetle.name: Elm Leaf Beetle
elm-beetle.description: The elm leaf beetle skeletonizes elm tree leaves and is a significant urban pest. Adults often overwinter inside buildings, emerging in spring to feed on newly emerged elm leaves.

fire-ant.name: Red Imported Fire Ant
fire-ant.description: Red imported fire ants are invasive ants native to South America that deliver painful stings causing burning welts. They build large mound nests and can survive flooding by forming floating colonies.

leafcutter-ant.name: Leafcutter Ant
leafcutter-ant.description: Leafcutter ants cut and carry pieces of leaves back to their nests to feed a special fungus that they cultivate. They are sophisticated farmers with complex division of labor among castes.

bullet-ant.name: Bullet Ant
bullet-ant.description: The bullet ant gets its name from the intense pain of its sting, which has been compared to being shot. Indigenous tribes use bullet ant stings in coming-of-age rituals.
bullet-ant.funFact: La hormiga con la picadura más dolorosa

army-ant.name: Army Ant
army-ant.description: Army ants are nomadic predators that form massive raiding swarms. They do not build permanent nests but instead form living bivouacs made of their own bodies while the colony rests.

trap-jaw-ant.name: Trap-Jaw Ant
trap-jaw-ant.description: Trap-jaw ants have spring-loaded mandibles that snap shut at incredible speeds to capture prey and can also use the force to launch themselves into the air to escape predators.

weaver-ant.name: Weaver Ant
weaver-ant.description: Weaver ants build elaborate nests by weaving living leaves together using silk produced by their larvae. They are aggressive defenders of their territory and tend honeydew-producing insects.

honeybee.name: Western Honeybee
honeybee.description: The western honeybee is the world's most important pollinator of agricultural crops. They live in highly organized colonies with complex social structures and produce honey and beeswax.

bumblebee.name: Common Bumblebee
bumblebee.description: Bumblebees are robust, fuzzy bees important for pollinating wildflowers and crops. They are capable of buzz pollination, vibrating their flight muscles to release pollen from flowers.

carpenter-bee.name: Eastern Carpenter Bee
carpenter-bee.description: Carpenter bees are large, solitary bees that bore into untreated wood to create nesting tunnels. Despite their intimidating size, they are gentle and rarely sting, preferring to hover near structures.

paper-wasp.name: European Paper Wasp
paper-wasp.description: Paper wasps are slender wasps with long legs that build open-comb umbrella-shaped nests from wood pulp. They are beneficial predators of caterpillars but will sting if their nest is threatened.

yellow-jacket.name: Common Yellow Jacket
yellow-jacket.description: Yellow jackets are aggressive wasps known for their bright yellow and black markings. They build enclosed paper nests and are notorious for scavenging at picnics and outdoor events.

bald-faced-hornet.name: Bald-Faced Hornet
bald-faced-hornet.description: Despite its name, the bald-faced hornet is actually a yellowjacket, not a true hornet. It builds large, enclosed paper nests high in trees and is known for its aggressive defense of its colony.

european-hornet.name: European Hornet
european-hornet.description: The European hornet is the largest social wasp in Europe and an invasive species in North America. Queens can reach 1.4 inches in length, and colonies can contain up to 1,000 workers.

tarantula-hawk-wasp.name: Tarantula Hawk Wasp
tarantula-hawk-wasp.description: The tarantula hawk is a large, metallic blue-black wasp that hunts tarantulas to serve as live food for its larvae. Its sting is excruciatingly painful but rarely dangerous to humans.

cuckoo-wasp.name: Cuckoo Wasp
cuckoo-wasp.description: Cuckoo wasps are brilliant metallic blue or green parasitoids that lay their eggs in the nests of other bees and wasps. Their larvae consume the host's eggs or larvae and stored food.

ichneumon-wasp.name: Giant Ichneumon Wasp
ichneumon-wasp.description: Giant ichneumon wasps are parasitoids that use their extremely long ovipositors to drill into wood and lay eggs inside wood-boring beetle larvae. Despite their fearsome appearance, they cannot sting humans.

asian-giant-hornet.name: Asian Giant Hornet
asian-giant-hornet.description: The Asian giant hornet, nicknamed the murder hornet, is the world's largest hornet. Its powerful sting delivers potent venom and it is a devastating predator of honeybee colonies.
asian-giant-hornet.funFact: El abejorro más grande del mundo

sweat-bee.name: Sweat Bee
sweat-bee.description: Sweat bees are small, often metallic-colored bees attracted to human perspiration for its salt content. They are important pollinators and nest in the ground or in hollow stems.

mason-bee.name: Blue Orchard Mason Bee
mason-bee.description: The blue orchard mason bee is a solitary bee that nests in hollow tubes and crevices. It is a far more efficient pollinator than honeybees, visiting far more flowers per hour.

mining-bee.name: Tawny Mining Bee
mining-bee.description: Mining bees are solitary ground-nesting bees that excavate tunnels in soil. They emerge in spring and are important early-season pollinators of fruit trees and wildflowers.

golden-digger-wasp.name: Golden Digger Wasp
golden-digger-wasp.description: The golden digger wasp is a large, metallic golden wasp that hunts grasshoppers and crickets. It buries paralyzed prey in underground nests for its developing larvae.

mud-dauber-wasp.name: Mud Dauber Wasp
mud-dauber-wasp.description: Mud dauber wasps are solitary wasps that construct tubular mud nests on sheltered surfaces. They hunt and paralyze spiders to stock each cell for their developing young.

horned-mason-bee.name: Horned Mason Bee
horned-mason-bee.description: The horned mason bee is a solitary bee that nests in hollow stems and bee hotels. Males have distinctive facial horns and both sexes are important early-season pollinators.

wool-carder-bee.name: Wool Carder Bee
wool-carder-bee.description: Wool carder bees are solitary bees that collect plant hairs to line their nest cells. Males aggressively defend patches of fuzzy plants where females forage for nesting material.

cicada-killer-wasp.name: Cicada Killer Wasp
cicada-killer-wasp.description: The cicada killer is a massive solitary wasp that hunts cicadas to provision its underground nest. Despite its intimidating size, it rarely stings humans unless provoked.
cicada-killer-wasp.funFact: La avispia más grande de Norteamérica

red-velvet-ant.name: Red Velvet Ant
red-velvet-ant.description: The red velvet ant is a wingless female wasp with a dense covering of bright red hairs. Despite its ant-like appearance, it is a parasitoid wasp whose sting is extremely painful.

cuckoo-bumblebee.name: Cuckoo Bumblebee
cuckoo-bumblebee.description: Cuckoo bumblebees are social parasites that take over the nests of other bumblebee species. The female cuckoo bumblebee displaces the host queen and lays her own eggs for the workers to tend.

mosquito.name: Asian Tiger Mosquito
mosquito.description: The Asian tiger mosquito is an invasive species that can transmit dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses. It is identified by its distinctive black and white striped body and legs.
mosquito.funFact: El insecto más mortal del mundo

house-fly.name: Common House Fly
house-fly.description: The common house fly is one of the most widespread insects, closely associated with humans. It has sponging mouthparts for liquid feeding and can transmit numerous diseases.

fruit-fly.name: Common Fruit Fly
fruit-fly.description: The common fruit fly is tiny but remarkably important in scientific research. They reproduce rapidly and share many genes with humans, making them invaluable for studying genetics and disease.

crane-fly.name: Crane Fly
crane-fly.description: Crane flies are delicate, long-legged insects that resemble oversized mosquitoes. Adults are harmless and many do not feed at all, while their larvae, known as leatherjackets, live in soil.

horsefly.name: Horse Fly
horsefly.description: Horse flies are large, powerful fliers with razor-sharp mouthparts that slash skin to feed on blood. Only females bite, and their painful bites can transmit diseases to livestock and humans.

bot-fly.name: Human Bot Fly
bot-fly.description: The human bot fly is a parasitic insect whose larvae develop beneath the skin of mammals, including humans. Adults do not bite; instead, they hijack mosquitoes to deliver their eggs to hosts.

hover-fly.name: Common Hover Fly
hover-fly.description: Hover flies are beneficial pollinators that mimic the appearance of stinging insects for protection. Their larvae are important predators of aphids, making them valuable in pest control.

black-fly.name: Black Fly
black-fly.description: Black flies are tiny but relentless biting insects that breed in flowing water. In some regions they transmit river blindness and are considered one of the most important disease vectors.

damselfly.name: Blue-Tailed Damselfly
damselfly.description: Damselflies are slender, delicate relatives of dragonflies that hold their wings together above their body when resting. They are important aquatic ecosystem indicators and voracious mosquito predators.

blue-dasher-dragonfly.name: Blue Dasher Dragonfly
blue-dasher-dragonfly.description: The blue dasher is a small, common dragonfly with a blue-green body and distinctive wing pattern. It is an agile aerial predator that catches mosquitoes and other small insects on the wing.

emperor-dragonfly.name: Emperor Dragonfly
emperor-dragonfly.description: The emperor dragonfly is one of the largest and most powerful dragonflies in Europe. It patrols territories over water and feeds voraciously on mosquitoes, flies, and other flying insects.
emperor-dragonfly.funFact: La libélula más grande de Europa

four-spotted-chaser.name: Four-Spotted Chaser
four-spotted-chaser.description: The four-spotted chaser is a robust dragonfly with distinctive dark spots on its wings. It is an aggressive territorial species that perches on vegetation to ambush passing prey.

robber-fly.name: Robber Fly
robber-fly.description: Robber flies are aerial predators that intercept prey in flight. They inject victims with saliva that paralyzes and digests their insides, then suck out the liquefied contents.

marmalade-hoverfly.name: Marmalade Hoverfly
marmalade-hoverfly.description: The marmalade hoverfly is a bee-mimic hoverfly that is an important pollinator. Its larvae are voracious aphid predators, making it doubly valuable in gardens and agriculture.

common-mosquito.name: Common Mosquito
common-mosquito.description: Mosquitoes are small, buzzing flies that transmit deadly diseases including malaria, dengue, and Zika. Only females bite to obtain blood for egg production, while males feed on nectar.

biting-midge.name: Biting Midge
biting-midge.description: Biting midges are tiny flies that deliver disproportionately painful bites. They are among the smallest biting flies and can be major pests in coastal and tropical regions.

deer-fly.name: Deer Fly
deer-fly.description: Deer flies are fast-flying, aggressive biters with patterned wings. They transmit tularemia and can cause severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

cattle-bot-fly.name: Cattle Bot Fly
cattle-bot-fly.description: The cattle bot fly is a parasitic fly whose larvae develop in the throats of cattle. Adults are bee-like in appearance and do not feed, living only long enough to reproduce.

orchid-mantis.name: Orchid Mantis
orchid-mantis.description: The orchid mantis is a stunning pink and white mantis that mimics orchid flowers to ambush pollinators. It is considered one of the most beautiful insects in the world.

ghost-mantis.name: Ghost Mantis
ghost-mantis.description: The ghost mantis is a master of camouflage with a body shaped and colored to resemble a dried leaf. It sways gently to mimic a leaf in the wind, hiding from both predators and prey.

leaf-mantis.name: Dead Leaf Mantis
leaf-mantis.description: The dead leaf mantis is a large, spectacular mantis with a flattened body resembling a dead leaf. It is an ambush predator that waits motionless for prey to come within striking distance.

walking-stick.name: Common Walking Stick
walking-stick.description: Walking sticks are elongated, camouflaged insects that resemble twigs or branches. They are nocturnal herbivores that rely on their extraordinary disguise to avoid detection by predators.

giant-walking-stick.name: Giant Walking Stick
giant-walking-stick.description: The giant walking stick, also known as Chan's megastick, is the longest insect species, with females reaching over 14 inches including legs. It is native to Borneo's tropical rainforests.

american-cockroach.name: American Cockroach
american-cockroach.description: The American cockroach is the largest common cockroach found in human habitations. Despite its name, it originated in Africa and is now found worldwide in warm, moist environments.

german-cockroach.name: German Cockroach
german-cockroach.description: The German cockroach is the most troublesome indoor cockroach species worldwide. It reproduces rapidly, is resistant to many insecticides, and contaminates food and surfaces with pathogens.

madagascar-hissing-cockroach.name: Madagascar Hissing Cockroach
madagascar-hissing-cockroach.description: The Madagascar hissing cockroach is one of the largest cockroach species, reaching 3 inches long. It is famous for the loud hissing sound it produces when disturbed, used for defense and communication.

oriental-cockroach.name: Oriental Cockroach
oriental-cockroach.description: The oriental cockroach is a large, dark species that prefers cool, damp environments. It is a scavenger that feeds on decaying organic matter and is associated with poor sanitation.

eastern-subterranean-termite.name: Eastern Subterranean Termite
eastern-subterranean-termite.description: Eastern subterranean termites are the most destructive termite species in North America. They live in underground colonies and build mud tubes to reach wood structures above ground.

formosan-termite.name: Formosan Subterranean Termite
formosan-termite.description: The Formosan termite is one of the most destructive termite species, capable of consuming enormous amounts of wood. Unlike most termites, it can build above-ground nests, making it especially destructive.

dampwood-termite.name: Dampwood Termite
dampwood-termite.description: Dampwood termites infest moist, decaying wood and are indicators of excessive moisture problems. They are larger than subterranean termites and do not build mud tubes.

drywood-termite.name: Drywood Termite
drywood-termite.description: Drywood termites live entirely within the wood they consume and do not require soil contact. They are difficult to detect and treat because colonies can be scattered throughout a structure.

cicada.name: Periodical Cicada
cicada.description: Periodical cicadas are famous for their synchronized mass emergences every 13 or 17 years. They are the longest-lived insects and their emergences create deafening choruses heard for miles.
cicada.funFact: Un insecto que canta en verano

dog-day-cicada.name: Dog-Day Cicada
dog-day-cicada.description: Dog-day cicadas are annual cicadas that emerge each summer, unlike their periodical cousins. Their loud buzzing songs fill late summer afternoons in eastern North America.
dog-day-cicada.funFact: La cigarra de los días calurosos

masked-devil-cicada.name: Masked Devil Cicada
masked-devil-cicada.description: The masked devil cicada is an Australian species known for its distinctive facial markings. Like other cicadas, it spends years underground before emerging for a brief, noisy adult life.

leafhopper.name: Brown Planthopper
leafhopper.description: The brown planthopper is a major pest of rice crops in Asia. It feeds on plant sap and transmits the devastating rice ragged stunt virus and rice grassy stunt virus.

spittlebug.name: Meadow Spittlebug
spittlebug.description: Spittlebugs get their name from the frothy foam masses their nymphs produce on plant stems. These nymphs, called froghoppers, are sap-sucking insects that can transmit plant diseases.

aphid.name: Green Peach Aphid
aphid.description: The green peach aphid is one of the most destructive agricultural pests worldwide. It reproduces rapidly through asexual reproduction and transmits over 100 plant viruses.

bed-bug.name: Common Bed Bug
bed-bug.description: Bed bugs are parasitic insects that feed on human blood at night. They hide in mattress seams, furniture, and wall cracks, and their populations have surged worldwide due to pesticide resistance.

kissing-bug.name: Triatomine Bug
kissing-bug.description: Triatomine bugs, also known as kissing bugs, are vectors of Chagas disease. They feed on blood at night and transmit the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi through their feces.

stink-bug.name: Brown Marmorated Stink Bug
stink-bug.description: The brown marmorated stink bug is an invasive species from Asia that has become a major agricultural pest in North America. It damages fruit crops and invades homes in winter seeking shelter.

box-elder-bug.name: Box Elder Bug
box-elder-bug.description: Box elder bugs are black insects with red markings that feed on box elder tree seeds. They become nuisances in fall when they cluster on buildings seeking warmth for winter.

water-strider.name: Common Water Strider
water-strider.description: Water striders are insects that glide across the surface of calm water using surface tension. Their hydrophobic leg hairs create air cushions that keep them afloat while they hunt prey.

giant-water-bug.name: Giant Water Bug
giant-water-bug.description: Giant water bugs are large, flat-bodied aquatic predators that prey on fish, frogs, and snakes. Males carry eggs on their backs and are sometimes called electric-light bugs for their attraction to lights.

american-grasshopper.name: American Bird Grasshopper
american-grasshopper.description: The American bird grasshopper is a large, strong-flying grasshopper that feeds on a wide variety of plants. It gets its name from its bird-like flight and large size.

desert-locust.name: Desert Locust
desert-locust.description: The desert locust is the most destructive of all locust species. Under certain conditions it transforms from a solitary grasshopper into a gregarious swarming phase capable of devastating crops.

mormon-cricket.name: Mormon Cricket
mormon-cricket.description: The Mormon cricket is not a cricket but a large shield-backed katydid that forms migrating bands of billions. They were named after Mormon settlers whose crops they devastated in the 1840s.

field-cricket.name: Field Cricket
field-cricket.description: Field crickets are known for their distinctive chirping songs produced by males to attract mates. They are omnivorous scavengers that feed on plants, fungi, and other insects.

katydid.name: True Katydid
katydid.description: True katydids are named after their call, said to sound like Katy-did, Katy-didn't. They are leaf-mimicking insects that produce loud, clicking songs at ultrasonic frequencies.

mole-cricket.name: European Mole Cricket
mole-cricket.description: Mole crickets are burrowing insects with powerful, shovel-like forelegs adapted for digging through soil. They damage lawns and crops by feeding on roots and disrupting soil structure.

snowy-tree-cricket.name: Snowy Tree Cricket
snowy-tree-cricket.description: The snowy tree cricket produces a pure, musical trill and is famous for its temperature-dependent chirping rate. Dolbear's Law uses its chirps to estimate ambient temperature.

human-head-louse.name: Human Head Louse
human-head-louse.description: Human head lice are parasitic insects that live on the scalp and feed on blood. They are wingless and highly adapted to life on humans, spreading through direct head-to-head contact.
human-head-louse.funFact: El piojo de la cabeza humana

body-louse.name: Human Body Louse
body-louse.description: Human body lice live in clothing and emerge to feed on blood. Unlike head lice, they can transmit serious diseases including typhus, trench fever, and relapsing fever.

human-flea.name: Human Flea
human-flea.description: The human flea, Pulex irritans, is the original flea species associated with humans. It is a blood-feeding parasite that can transmit diseases and has been a companion of humans for millennia.

cat-flea.name: Cat Flea
cat-flea.description: The cat flea is the most common flea species affecting domestic cats and dogs. Despite its name, it infests many mammal species and can cause allergic dermatitis and transmit tapeworms.

oriental-rat-flea.name: Oriental Rat Flea
oriental-rat-flea.description: The oriental rat flea is historically the most important disease vector among fleas, having transmitted bubonic plague during the Black Death. It feeds primarily on rats and other rodents.
oriental-rat-flea.funFact: La pulga oriental de la rata

brown-recluse-spider.name: Brown Recluse Spider
brown-recluse-spider.description: The brown recluse spider has a violin-shaped marking on its cephalothorax and venom that can cause tissue death. It is reclusive and bites only when pressed against skin.

wolf-spider.name: Common Wolf Spider
wolf-spider.description: Wolf spiders are agile, ground-hunting spiders that do not build webs. They have excellent vision and chase down their prey, and females are notable for carrying their young on their backs.

jumping-spider.name: Bold Jumping Spider
jumping-spider.description: Bold jumping spiders are charismatic, fuzzy spiders with large forward-facing eyes. They are active hunters that stalk prey and leap to capture it, displaying complex courtship dances.

orb-weaver-spider.name: Garden Orb Weaver Spider
orb-weaver-spider.description: Garden orb weavers are among the most common web-building spiders. They create distinctive circular webs and are beneficial predators of flying insects in gardens and natural areas.

peacock-spider.name: Peacock Spider
peacock-spider.description: Peacock spiders are tiny jumping spiders famous for the males' spectacular iridescent abdominal flaps used in elaborate courtship dances. Females will eat males who fail to impress.

brazilian-wandering-spider.name: Brazilian Wandering Spider
brazilian-wandering-spider.description: The Brazilian wandering spider is considered the world's most venomous spider. Unlike web-building spiders, it actively wanders the forest floor at night and can deliver a medically significant bite.
brazilian-wandering-spider.funFact: La araña más venenosa del mundo

emperor-scorpion.name: Emperor Scorpion
emperor-scorpion.description: The emperor scorpion is one of the largest scorpion species and one of the most popular in the pet trade. Despite its intimidating size, its venom is relatively mild and it is generally docile.
emperor-scorpion.funFact: El escorpión más grande del mundo

bark-scorpion.name: Arizona Bark Scorpion
bark-scorpion.description: The Arizona bark scorpion is the most dangerous scorpion in North America. It is unique among scorpions in its ability to climb walls and ceilings, often entering homes through plumbing.

deathstalker-scorpion.name: Deathstalker Scorpion
deathstalker-scorpion.description: The deathstalker is one of the most venomous scorpions in the world. Its potent neurotoxic venom can be fatal to humans, but its venom compounds show promise in medical research.

spotted-lanternfly.name: Spotted Lanternfly
spotted-lanternfly.description: The spotted lanternfly is an invasive planthopper from Asia that feeds on over 70 plant species, threatening agriculture. Adults have distinctive spotted wings and bright red hind wings.

wheel-bug.name: Wheel Bug
wheel-bug.description: The wheel bug is a large, beneficial predatory insect with a distinctive semicircular crest on its thorax. It uses its proboscis to inject digestive enzymes into prey and is a natural pest controller.

sawfly.name: Rose Slug Sawfly
sawfly.description: Sawflies are wasp-like insects whose larvae feed on plant foliage, resembling caterpillars. The rose slug sawfly can skeletonize rose leaves, causing significant damage to gardens.

antlion.name: Antlion
antlion.description: Antlions are insects whose larvae are famous for digging conical pitfall traps in sand. They wait at the bottom of the pit for prey to fall in, then inject digestive enzymes.

lacewing.name: Green Lacewing
